title: Sunny and the Cloud Shapes
description: Little Sonny the quokka lies on his back and watches the clouds slowly drift and change shape. A dreamy, peaceful bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
One afternoon, Sunny lay on his back in the soft warm grass and looked up.

The sky was very blue. And across it, slow and steady and unhurried, drifted a long procession of clouds.

Sunny looked at the first one. It was fat and round at the bottom and puffed up high in the middle. He tilted his head. It looked a little bit like a wombat sitting up very straight, which made him smile.

The next cloud was long and wispy, like someone had stretched it out gently from both ends. Like a sleeping cat. Or maybe a scarf, left floating in the sky.

Sunny watched a third cloud slowly arrive from the edge of the sky. This one was large and complicated, with big billowing sections and smaller trails coming off it. He couldn't decide what it looked like. Something between a whale and a very large island. He decided to call it both.

He didn't really need to name them. He just liked noticing them.

The clouds moved slowly, slowly, changing shape as they went. The wombat cloud lost its head and became something rounder. The cat cloud stretched into a long thin line and faded.

Sunny watched the whole parade, his paws folded on his chest, his eyes soft and easy.

The sun was warm on his face. The grass was cool beneath him.

He didn't fall asleep, exactly. He just floated somewhere between awake and dreaming, watching the slow, slow drift of clouds across the wide blue sky.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, quiet clouds. Goodnight, wide and dreaming sky.
